name: Nazi-Maoism
summary: Nazi-Maoism is a small Italian, then European, current of the late 1960s and 1970s that tried to fuse far-right racial and elitist ideas with Maoist people's war and an anti-bourgeois, anti-Western stance. Its theorist Franco Freda sought a 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat' that would destroy the bourgeois liberal system, abolish private property, and rebuild a totalitarian, hierarchical state under a philosopher-elite.
scope: Represents the Italian Lotta di Popolo milieu (1968-73) and Franco Freda's writings (The Disintegration of the System, 1969, and the Gruppo di Ar manifesto), with the French Lutte du Peuple and Thiriart-circle 'fascist Maoism' as related branches. Excludes later Eurasianist and Azov-linked revivals and other third-position groups such as Strasserism or National Bolshevism. Evidence is thin and mostly secondary, so many answers are inferences.

sources.title: The Disintegration of the System (PhD thesis abstract, Freda's terrorism 1969-1979)
sources.author: University of Northampton
sources.usedFor: Scholarly characterization of Freda as Platonic and Evolian, anti-state, anti-democratic, and of armed struggle as a minority's response.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call for state ownership of all material wealth; a state that owns everything would provide basic services, though healthcare is never discussed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A wage floor is a reformist capitalist device; adherents want to abolish the bourgeois order rather than adjust pay within it, so the issue is not really theirs.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Freda demanded that all material wealth belong to the state and that the bourgeois capitalist order be destroyed, so market allocation is rejected outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Freda's Disintegration of the System says material wealth must be state property and private property in all forms eliminated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation as such is not discussed; a movement aiming at abolishing private property and bourgeois wealth would endorse heavy burdens on the rich as a stopgap.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: the group rejects class-struggle reformism and parties of the system, and a fascist proletarian state would subordinate unions to itself; no direct statement found.

property-fundamental.rationale: Freda said elimination of private property in all its forms is necessary.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: adherents want corporations abolished into state enterprises, so tighter regulation is a weaker form of what they already demand.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the state-owns-everything economy and the 'people's state' rhetoric; welfare cuts as a free-market move are opposed, though no welfare policy is documented.

worker-ownership.rationale: Property is to be owned by the state, not by workers collectively, in Freda's scheme of state enterprises and agricultural combines under commissars.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: a totalitarian state that sees itself as absolute would accept surveillance; terrorism-prevention framing is anachronistic and the group itself used terror.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Freda's Spartan, warrior ethos and Evolian hierarchy, which treat purity and discipline as virtues; drugs are not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are themselves antisemitic and would reject liberal speech law, but a totalitarian state would censor too; the answer is inferred from their rejection of liberal democratic rights.

strong-leader.rationale: Freda envisaged a hierarchical, collectivist state ruled by a philosopher-elite and a vanguard, rejecting parliamentary gridlock and parties.

state-harmful.rationale: Freda held the state to be an organic, totalitarian and eternal absolute, the opposite of anarchist rejection of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: a movement preparing people's war and armed struggle would not favor strictly limiting gun ownership among its own, though the state would monopolize force.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian state ideal and warrior ethos; funding of police is not specifically addressed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Spartan, ascetic style Freda praised and Evolian traditionalism; not stated.

decide-locally.rationale: Freda's state is an organic, totalitarian absolute, which implies central authority rather than local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Freda proposed forced-labor penal measures and said purity justifies any hardness, pointing to punishment over rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Evolian traditionalism and hierarchy that Freda's circle published imply traditional family, but family policy is not documented for the group.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Evola-inspired traditionalism and neofascist background; no direct statement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the neofascist, traditionalist milieu; not documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: Freda opposed Christianity for its universalism and egalitarianism and championed neopaganism, so a larger public role for the established religion is rejected.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Freda called himself a scholar of ethnicity with a 'morphological racism' and admired Hitler; remedial anti-racism runs against that.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist and racial-biological outlook of the Ar circle; not stated.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The group aimed at a European rebirth against Judaized, liberal Europe rather than at national traditions as such, and also drew on foreign models like China and Vietnam.

gradual-change.rationale: Freda called for destruction of the bourgeois world and Maoist people's war, not gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Fronte Nazionale, Freda's later group, opposed globalization and multicultural society; the earlier Nazi-Maoist groups left immigration unaddressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents were violently anti-American, rejected liberal internationalism and the post-war order, and called for European independence.

free-trade.rationale: Rejection of capitalism and of the American-imposed liberal order makes free trade unwelcome; trade policy itself is not documented.

nation-first.rationale: Lutte du Peuple and Freda's circle called for a separate, heroic Europe against the West and America; Europe rather than the nation is the unit, but the anti-global-cooperation stance holds.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The movement was anti-American, anti-liberal and dismissed human-rights universalism; Western interventions are rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from ethnic racism and opposition to a multicultural society in the Freda tradition.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits are not discussed; Freda's ascetic rhetoric against bourgeois mercantilism is not an ecological programme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic: no position on climate in the 1968-73 groups; a totalitarian state could act drastically, but this is not documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from Evola-influenced revulsion against the modern bourgeois world; technology is not discussed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no principle clearly points either way.

revolution-justified.rationale: The core programme was revolution by Maoist people's war and armed struggle against the government and bourgeoisie.

experts-over-public.rationale: Freda wanted a philosopher-ruler elite chosen for moral and spiritual qualities; this is rule by a qualified few rather than technocratic expertise.

central-planning.rationale: State ownership of all material wealth, state enterprises and agricultural combines under commissars imply comprehensive state direction of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets are not part of the programme, which wants state property; owners-as-state markets are not discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single-tax scheme is not part of a programme to abolish private property in land; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Abolition of private property in all forms would eliminate inheritance of wealth, so heavy taxation is a weaker version of their view; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a state owning all wealth might guarantee subsistence, but the Spartan emphasis on work and hardness cuts against unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from state control of the economy and hostility to the Western liberal market order.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State enterprises and state ownership of all material wealth entail the state directing investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Private property is to be eliminated, and the bourgeois small owner was called the worst evil in Italy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme abolishes private property but proposes forced labor and state enterprises, not a wageless society; no statement about money was found.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-run economy would keep central control of money; the free-market premise of abolition is rejected.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Freda's circle was fascist yet rejected corporatist settlements as compromise with the system and attacked the MSI for such compromises; evidence is indirect.

one-party-rule.rationale: Freda said 'we are against political parties' yet favored a vanguard party leading and administering the people, so the answer is genuinely split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Freda's elite is a philosopher-ruler class chosen by quality, not hereditary right; monarchy is not addressed directly.

democracy-best.rationale: Freda's manifesto: 'We are antidemocratic: above the fetishes of capitalist and Bolshevik democracy.'

direct-votes.rationale: Electoral politics was seen as irreformable and the group rejected democratic procedures; a 'people's state' is not plebiscitary in documents found.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is to rest with a hierarchical state and vanguard rather than with councils; Freda explicitly rejected parliaments and parties but not in favor of councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from the organic, totalitarian and absolute view of the state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Freda proposed a philosopher-ruler elite drawn from Plato and Evola, chosen for moral and spiritual qualities.

political-violence-never.rationale: The doctrine centered on people's war, terrorism and acceleration of the system's collapse; Freda saw armed struggle as the response of a marginalized minority.

war-builds-character.rationale: Freda praised the warrior people of North Vietnam for their Spartan, heroic style and said purity justifies any hardness, in an Evolian warrior ethos.

separate-church-state.rationale: Opposition to Christianity and promotion of paganism does not give a clear stance on formal separation; the state is totalitarian over all spheres.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Freda opposed Christianity, championed Nietzsche and neopaganism, and grounded the state in Plato, Gentile and Evola rather than scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is an absolute, totalitarian organism that holds all authority, so privatized courts and defense are ruled out.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the warrior ethos and anti-American stance; the group never governed, and military policy for Europe was not detailed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Freda described himself as a scholar of ethnicity and proposed a 'morphological racism', and wanted Europe cleansed of Judaized influence.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The group used Maoist class-struggle and people's war against the bourgeoisie, but Freda's state theory rejected the Marxist reduction of state to class conflict and added race and spirit.

equal-outcomes.rationale: A hierarchical, elitist state is not egalitarian, though material wealth is to be collectively held; Freda opposed Christianity for egalitarianism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the group; they did admire anti-Western fighters but no stance on this issue was found.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; anti-Western rhetoric might favor it, but the racial outlook cuts against.

civilizational-union.rationale: Lutte du Peuple called for 'European Socialism' and Freda wanted a reawakened Europe, and Thiriart-style circles sought a united Europe.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Selfishness is bourgeois; Freda's ethic prizes Spartan sobriety, heroism and subordination to the state.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Freda said the true state is not a simple structure of positive rights; duty and the organic state come first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Evolian traditionalism and neopaganism might favor it, but no direct evidence.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the sources found.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Freda attacked bourgeois mercantile modernity yet his programme used state enterprises and collectivized agriculture; no stance on industrial civilization as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the Evolian, anti-modern outlook; accelerationism here concerned collapse of the system, not technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; neither principle clearly applies.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; Freda's rulers are philosopher-elites chosen by spiritual quality, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; totalitarian state would not accept secrecy from itself, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Freda drew on Evola's tradition and called for rebirth yet also proposed a revolution on Maoist lines, so restoration versus progress splits.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Freda's creed holds that purity justifies any hardness; adherents are strongly ideological and reject pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: They rejected elections and parliaments and pursued armed struggle, terrorism and mass-line agitation.

means-match-ends.rationale: Freda said purity justifies any hardness and any deceit, and proposed false-flag operations, so means need not mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not an aim; the programme builds a state with enterprises and collectivized farms.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Freda's state is hierarchical with commissars and an elite, which implies division of labor; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No distribution principle was documented, and the Spartan hierarchy cuts against pure need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: The capitalist profit motive is rejected and wealth is state property, which suggests production for collective ends; not stated precisely.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The group attacked the bourgeoisie as the main enemy, but whether via Marxian exploitation theory is not documented, and Freda rejected Marxist state theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Freda's declared goal was a 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat' achieved by Maoist people's war, while mixing in race and elitism.

collective-farming.rationale: Freda proposed agricultural combines run by commissars, as the Fascio post notes, resembling Soviet collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Opposition to capitalism and imperialism is clear, but the inevitability claim is not documented.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation as theft is a libertarian claim; the state is absolute and owns all material wealth.

harm-principle.rationale: A totalitarian state directing all areas of life rejects limiting itself to preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Freda denied the state is a structure of positive rights, and adopted an organic, collective view.

conscription.rationale: A warrior-ethos totalitarian state would conscript; this is inferred from Freda's praise of Spartan, heroic style rather than an explicit program.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The absolute organic state and anti-liberalism contradict exit as a check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is to be an eternal, organic, absolute entity with state ownership, not a customer-service business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; liberty talk is liberal and the group rejected it, though material provision by the state is implied.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anti-liberal Europe-centered movements blame a liberal establishment, but this particular claim is not documented for them.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Freda's 'morphological racism' and admiration for Hitler imply biological racial difference, though the sources give few details.

organic-representation.rationale: They rejected parties and had an organic idea of the state, but a representative system through families and trades is not documented.

total-state.rationale: Freda saw the state as organic, totalitarian and absolute, directing all areas of life and the economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Freda's programme was a heroic reawakening of Europe against a decadent bourgeois, liberal, Judaized order.

territorial-expansion.rationale: A European power block was envisaged but expansion of territory is not documented; fascist inclinations are balanced by anti-imperialism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: elite chosen for qualities, not feudal personal oaths, though Freda took Evolian ideas about the Imperium.

bound-labor.rationale: Freda proposed forced-labor penal measures and commissars over collectives, resembling serfdom in form, but not lord-bound tenure.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; their rejection of liberal science as bourgeois is plausible but not documented.

universal-morality.rationale: Freda rejected Christian and liberal universalism and egalitarianism, favoring a hierarchical ethic of peoples and heroic virtue.

single-common-good.rationale: The organic, totalitarian state and rejection of parties imply one collective good set by the elite rather than interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Freda said 'we only have accounts to settle with the Jewish or Judaized Europe', and adherents were violently anti-Zionist.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from ethnic-nationalist racism and anti-Zionism; not directly stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: The sources show no language policy; their focus was a European, not a single-nation, rebirth.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Companies pass to the state and are run by commissars, not by votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: a totalitarian state directing education would not hand it to parental choice.

economic-freedom.rationale: State ownership of all material wealth and rejection of capitalism deny economic freedom as a condition of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Freda wanted rulers chosen for moral and spiritual quality, but also hardness and coercion, so only a partial fit.

national-self-determination.rationale: They focused on Europe as a unit and supported anti-Western fighters, while admiring ethnic identity; a general principle is not documented.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-internationalist and violent, the movement would not defer to UN approval; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Freda championed Nietzsche, Evola and neopaganism and spiritual hierarchy, which prize will and myth over bare reason; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigration policy and welfare scope were not documented for the original groups.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Freda proposed forced labor penal measures and a Spartan work ethic, which suggests obligations to work; welfare not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: The group wanted destruction of the bourgeoisie, the worst evil in Italy, not partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Freda published and revered traditionalist and Evolian classics, but also wanted destruction of the bourgeois world; split but leaning against destroying heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Adherents were violently anti-American and admired North Vietnam, China and Palestinian militants as fronts against Western liberalism.

workers-nation.rationale: The programme fused proletarian revolution with nationalist and European identity, not an international working-class movement.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from Evola-influenced traditionalism and hierarchical ethos; not documented for the group.

ban-interest.rationale: Anti-bourgeois, anti-mercantile outlook and state control of wealth point that way; usury was not documented specifically.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Morphological racism and Judaized-Europe rhetoric imply racial separation, but no specific segregation law was documented.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Freda rejected the Marxist view of the state as a tool of class conflict, holding it to be an organic, eternal absolute.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is absent from the documented programme and no principle of theirs points either way.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Ethnic-racial outlook means assimilation is no solution, though immigration is not documented for these groups.

elite-replacement.rationale: Freda blamed Judaized and liberal elites for corrupting Europe, but the replacement theory is a later formulation and not documented for the original groups.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State ownership of all material wealth implies state price setting, though food price caps are not specifically documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: They rejected parties and elections as irreformable; no preference between electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Not documented; Europe's awakening is a mission but not an export of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist hierarchy; not discussed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They denounced the Italian republic as an agonizing democracy and the MSI for compromising with it, and parties as fetishes of the system.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial-biological thinking and Spartan models make this plausible, but no document on eugenics was found.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: an authoritarian state would resist legal accountability for its own forces; not documented.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is totalitarian and owns all material wealth, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Freda's morphological racism and his admiration for Hitler imply racial separateness; specific marriage policy was not found.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Freda opposed egalitarianism, favored hierarchical elites and racialist ideas, and wanted a Spartan, elitist society.

socialism-one-country.rationale: They accepted Maoist-type revolution in one setting and looked to Europe, with no theory of permanent world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-Zionist rhetoric of the Nazi-Maoists casts Israel as imperialist, yet the colonial-project framing is not cited.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A totalitarian unitary state would have one law; religion was not the subject.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is absent from the sources; hostility to Christianity gives no clear direction.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious question that the European movement never touched; no basis for an answer.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: They disliked Christianity and favored neopaganism, but education policy is not documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Totalitarian state-strengthening view is plausible given hostility to the West, but encirclement theory is not documented.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Their rejection of democracy and parties and elite rule by philosopher-rulers deny consent as a basis for authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantile trade strategy is not discussed; the group attacked mercantile liberal Europe without setting trade targets.

population-transfer.rationale: Anti-Jewish rhetoric and racial outlook make it plausible, but no transfer plan was documented.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Their programme was armed struggle and terror; they would reject a non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A Nietzschean, warrior ethos suggests struggle between peoples as vital, but economic competition is rejected; partial.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They were themselves outlawed extremists opposed to the republic, but a totalitarian state would ban rivals; split and inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty theory is a liberal framework that the group did not engage; a hierarchical totalitarian state denies it.

separated-powers.rationale: A state that is an organic, totalitarian absolute does not divide power into checking bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Fascio account says Freda favored a vanguard party that leads the people and administers, in line with Maoist and Bordigist influences.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Proletarian rhetoric exists but the ethic is hierarchical and elitist; no documented stance.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Private property is to be eliminated, so converting state housing into private ownership is opposed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; they wanted revolutionary upheaval but a totalitarian state would control labor action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is blamed on the bourgeois system; Malthusian explanation is not documented.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Racist ethnic outlook and later Fronte Nazionale opposition to multicultural society point this way.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Freda proposed rule by a chosen philosopher-elite, the opposite of sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Freda said purity justifies any hardness and any deceit and the state is absolute; legal protections are bourgeois.

party-controls-media.rationale: The totalitarian state directs culture, and a vanguard party leading the people would control information; stated indirectly.

party-commands-army.rationale: Maoist model of party command plus the vanguard concept suggests it, but this was not documented for the group.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They rejected representative government, so the question barely applies.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: A disciplined vanguard party in the Maoist and Leninist tradition, and Freda's 'purity and hardness', imply binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They wanted a heroic united Europe, but not the liberal-mercantile EU, which they saw as a system to destroy.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No constitutional design of command was documented.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Opposed to Christianity, so church governance is not a concern, and they'd not endorse bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Freda's rulers are philosopher-elites in Plato and Evola's mold and he opposed Christianity.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leninist revolutionary defeatism does not match the nationalist and European framing, and no stance was found.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: A totalitarian state directing culture and a call for cultural revolution against bourgeois values imply censorship for virtue.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A permanent leadership under a vanguard is consistent with their anti-electoral outlook.

recall-officials.rationale: Rejects electoral machinery, but a mass-line Maoist element is compatible with popular removal; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents were anti-American and sought European independence from the post-war liberal order, so NATO-style alliances would end.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private ownership of homes is not their aim; they would eliminate private property, so ownership by every family is contrary.

people-in-arms.rationale: Maoist people's war and guerrilla struggle imply an armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: They proposed collectivized agriculture and admired peasant-based people's war, but moral superiority of rural life was not documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No stance on divided nations was found in the sources, apart from admiration for North Vietnam.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Maoist cultural-revolution influence and mass-line suggests suspicion of intellectuals, but not stated explicitly.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Racial hierarchy and Eurocentric awakening differ from cultural relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Their ethic of hardness suggests approval, but nothing was documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Paganism and Nietzschean views conflict with Christian creationism; no education policy documented.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Spartan ethos and cultural revolution against bourgeois decadence suggest restriction; not documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic nation concept implies descent-based membership; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the unitary, ethnic-organic state.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A totalitarian state would not exempt minorities from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Their elitist, disciplined ethic of hardness and conformity to the organic state opposes eccentric individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-Western, anti-capitalist solidarity with dominated peoples suggests it, not directly documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-imperialist anti-capitalism fits, though not stated as such.

constituent-assembly.rationale: They rejected democracy and elections as irreformable.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from a totalitarian state; development is not their documented concern.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Universalist aid duty conflicts with their racial outlook, while anti-imperial rhetoric is sympathetic to the dominated; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anti-American European independence would imply it, but not documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state owning all wealth would control money, and independence from the government is a liberal principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Freda held that all material wealth belongs to the state, so property is subordinate to collective ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: They criticized the USSR as a rival model to China, but whether as state-capitalist is not documented.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for a 1968-73 group and is not documented.

collective-defense.rationale: Anti-NATO stance implies rejection of the alliance form, but a European collective defense might be accepted; split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions on annexation are not covered in the sources on the group.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: A totalitarian state over all areas and hostility to Christianity suggest subordination of church; not specifically documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state standing above parties as symbol is a constitutional device; the group wanted a vanguard-led state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from an absolute organic state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from unitary totalitarian state and collectivized economy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Evolian ideas of the Imperium invoke sacral authority, but divine descent for a head of state is not documented.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A programme of state ownership of all wealth has no place for a flat tax; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist-Maoist remolding of people conflicts with racial biologism; genuinely split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Freda saw the state as an absolute, not a structure of positive rights, and hardness justified by purity.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not mentioned in any source on the group, and no principle points either way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the philosopher-elite is not a mix with popular power; Plato's influence points to elite rule instead.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from Freda's totalitarian hierarchical state under an elite and the Maoist inheritance of revolutionary leadership; the sources do not discuss leader portraits directly.

equal-parenting.rationale: Never addressed; custody law is a bourgeois-system detail that adherents would not treat as a political question.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Mixed: the current borrowed Maoist language and hostility to the bourgeoisie, but fascist elements put race and the state above class.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist peasant-based line and its goal of abolishing private property.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the racial and elitist outlook, which gives little support to restoring displaced populations and their descendants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the pan-European and racial nationalism of the fascist-Maoist milieu, which put the race above existing borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from Freda's pagan, Evolian traditionalism and a totalitarian state; no source mentions punishing apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred; the current is not religious and no source shows a dress requirement for women.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the pan-European nation idea of the Thiriart-circle branches, which favoured continental union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the racial view of a European or Aryan community that should be united across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian, centralised state model, which leaves no room for self-governing minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from racial separatism and antisemitism in Freda's work, which reject minorities integrating on equal terms.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from Freda's idealist, traditionalist outlook, which puts spirit and the elite's will above economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cartels are not addressed; the current wanted to abolish private property, so the issue does not arise.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to the bourgeois liberal system, which an adherent would let fail rather than rescue.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The current wanted to destroy liberal institutions but rule by an elite, not by a national majority, so it does not simply side with majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, elitist and male-led totalitarian state; no source shows support for parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western, anti-bourgeois stance, which favours a closed Europe-centred or national economy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal international institutions and the system they support.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist emphasis on political will and ideological commitment, and the philosopher-elite's ethical mission.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Freda and the milieu embraced Maoist people's war and political violence by small groups to break the system.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mixed: the current wanted a hierarchical elite and an Evolian order, but of philosophers and not of birth; no source addresses titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the call to rebuild a hierarchical, Evolian-Platonic order and a European-civilizational identity against Americanism; history is not discussed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: adherents reject Western liberal 'civilizing' claims and back Third World anti-colonial struggle, though Freda's elitism favours hierarchy among peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a totalitarian, hierarchical state that forms its citizens; schooling for national loyalty is not stated.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from Freda's morphological racism and rejection of egalitarian doctrine; preferences for groups are not discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the demand that all material wealth belong to the state, which implies state control of money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Freda aimed to destroy the bourgeois liberal system through people's war, on the premise that it cannot be reformed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not documented; the milieu was anti-imperial and anti-American, while Eurasianist revivals are outside the scope.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the anti-American, anti-Western stance and Maoist Third-Worldism; no explicit delinking programme is documented.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist premise that the Western proletariat is bourgeoisified; Freda courted marginal and rebel groups rather than the established working class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A totalitarian state would not leave private owners free; Freda sought to abolish private property and impose state-set order.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Freda rejected liberal democracy and bourgeois legal guarantees in favour of a hierarchical state under a philosopher-elite.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the anti-bourgeois, anti-Western stance that rejected the post-war settlement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Freda sought a hierarchical elite state under a philosopher-elite and rejected liberal electoralism.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian, hierarchical state that crushes dissent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred; Freda sought to destroy the liberal constitutional system rather than operate within it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Freda sought the destruction of parliamentary liberal democracy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the elitist and hierarchical worldview that is indifferent to animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of bourgeois charity and the elite ethos of hardness and hierarchy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The current called for militant political action and people's war.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the anti-bourgeois and anti-Western critique of consumer culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the critique of the bourgeois system and its liberal ideology.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western, anti-bourgeois stance and Maoist influence.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the racial and elitist nationalism of the fascist half.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist idea of a separate road and anti-Soviet stance.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist self-reliance and rejection of the liberal international order.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; the strand was an Italian European revolutionary current with no stated claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the racial and elitist outlook that rejects equal-rights identity politics.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The current rejected anti-fascism and sought a 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat'.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The current embraced both the fascist and Maoist revolutionary models and rejected the liberal condemnation.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; an Italian current with no stated view on the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the far-right and revolutionary stance, with the current more iconoclastic than preserving.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, anti-liberal and anti-egalitarian worldview.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of liberal Western forms in favour of an own revolutionary state.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian, hierarchical state and people's war model, though the elite is philosophers.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, anti-egalitarian worldview.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Freda's Evolian and Platonic traditionalism and hierarchical state; no source discusses filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from Freda's Platonic ideal of rule by a philosopher-elite chosen by quality rather than by votes.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Freda wanted all material wealth owned by the state and an anti-American, anti-bourgeois order, so foreign buyers of firms would be barred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, hierarchical vision in Freda's thought; family law is never discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Freda called elections and parties fetishes of the bourgeois system and wanted a hierarchical elite state, not instructed delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Freda called for abolishing private property and state ownership of all material wealth, which leaves no room for private pension accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme of abolishing private property and state ownership of wealth implies land held by the nation rather than owned outright.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Freda sought to destroy the parliamentary liberal system and replace it with a totalitarian elite state, so parliamentary approval of spending is rejected.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the aim of a unitary totalitarian state with a single national culture.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of wealth and racial-nationalist exclusivity; no source states the position directly.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Freda held a 'morphological' racism and elitist hierarchy, rejecting egalitarian anti-discrimination frameworks.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nazi-Maoism was anti-bourgeois and anti-American, treating consumer society as a symptom of the system to be destroyed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist doctrine of people's war and support for armed struggle against the US-led order.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its anti-American, anti-Soviet and anti-hegemonic stance, which opposes superpower domination of other countries.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the movement's attack on the bourgeois liberal order and call for state ownership of wealth; corporate lobbying is never discussed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from its totalitarian, anti-American stance: a state that claims total authority would not let foreign money fund independent civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Freda's racial-elitist, hierarchical state, which would want the right stock to multiply; no incentive policy is documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: ownership of property is to pass to a centralised state, leaving no room for local authorities to decide who may buy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of all wealth and a mobilised, totalitarian economy, where the state would assign work; no explicit job guarantee is documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Adherents reject liberal democracy as a bourgeois system and are anti-Western, so spreading democracy is not a path to peace; the war claim itself is inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: a totalitarian state demands obedience, though adherents deny legitimacy to the existing liberal system and its laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-American, anti-imperialist rhetoric, though the movement backed people's war across borders so the absolute claim is loosely held.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: independent unions belong to the bourgeois system, and Freda wanted a hierarchical state organising labour from above.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Freda's texts and the movement's anti-Zionist, antisemitic strand cast Jews as a hostile force working against the nation and its people.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Freda's Evolian, traditionalist and hierarchical order, which would keep marriage and family as regulated institutions.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from a totalitarian, elite-led state that would keep its records closed; no statement on the issue is documented.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from its Maoist and anti-Western economics favouring self-reliance over integration into the world market.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Freda milieu aimed at a disciplined elite order, though it also used small clandestine cells; the statement's rejection of lasting formal organisation does not fit.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the Western liberal order and its institutions, which implies national sovereignty over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Its nation is defined by race and hierarchy rather than shared religion, with pagan and Evolian traditionalist influences.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its anti-American, anti-hegemonic stance and demand for European independence; tributary submission to any leading power runs against it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from a centralizing totalitarian state that owns all material wealth; regions keeping their own revenue is not a stated aim.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Freda demanded that all material wealth be state property and abolished private property in all forms, so a protected private sphere is not endorsed; personal items are never addressed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: the group fused Maoist and far-right ideas and opposed the Soviet and bourgeois orders alike, so it did not frame communism as the enemy to defeat.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from its demand for state ownership of all wealth and rejection of private enterprise; private providers in a public system conflict with this.

religion-illusion.rationale: Freda drew on Evolian traditionalism and a hierarchical sacral state, so religion is not treated as a mere illusion of material hardship; inferred, not stated directly.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Adherents saw the bourgeois capitalist order as the main enemy to be destroyed, not a stage that built a foundation; inferred from their anti-bourgeois texts.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Freda's hierarchical and traditionalist state would not centre women's equality, and the abolition of private property cuts the other way; adherents' view is not documented.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: a totalitarian state owning everything could socialize care, but the traditionalist family answer pulls the other way, and no source addresses it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The sources do not address language policy; a nationalist, anti-Western cultural stance might favour purism but this is not documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from a totalitarian state that rejects bourgeois legality and treaty-based restraints on state power; not addressed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Freda wanted a centralized, hierarchical totalitarian state under an elite, not small self-governing communes, though he rejected private property.

majority-settlement.rationale: The sources do not address internal settlement policy; ethnic-nation commitments hint at support but the movement is thin on this.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nazi-Maoism sought a 'third' synthesis of far-right and Maoist ideas that would destroy the bourgeois capitalist system while rejecting liberal democracy and Soviet-style communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the movement's racial and blood-based nationalism; the sources do not discuss land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from the Nazi side of the fusion and Freda's neo-Nazi milieu; the sources here do not state a position.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the movement's totalitarian, hierarchical and virility-minded fascism; not stated in the sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Freda sought a totalitarian state and declared 'We are antidemocratic' and against political parties.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Freda's esoteric, anti-Christian current gives no basis for state enforcement of a religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist anti-imperialist and anti-Western stance, though its racial hierarchy cuts the other way.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the milieu was anti-Western and sometimes sympathetic to Muslim resistance, but no doctrine on this duty is documented.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the movement wanted a secular philosopher-elite dictatorship, not rule by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Freda's design was a totalitarian, hierarchical state run by a philosopher-elite, with no role for popular decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement was elitist and racial-hierarchical and rejected egalitarian liberal and progressive frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, anti-liberal and far-right outlook; not stated in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources bears on it, and an elitist, anti-liberal movement gives no clear lead either way.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement's defining aim was to fuse far-right and Maoist ideas against the bourgeois liberal system.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from its anti-bourgeois, anti-capitalist stance and plan to abolish private property, though it did not use Marx's concept.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: its enemy was the bourgeois liberal West, not Islam, and it admired anti-Western movements.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: authority was to rest on a philosopher-elite and the state, not God or the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: no sourced position, and the totalitarian state would regulate dress at will.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to this employment-law issue; no position can be inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Freda wanted to destroy the bourgeois liberal system and abolish private property, rejecting both markets with safeguards and laissez-faire.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement embraced Maoist people's war and violent struggle and wanted a totalitarian state.

rich-first.rationale: Its anti-bourgeois, property-abolishing stance opposes letting some people grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to both the American-led West and Soviet-style communism, and its call for an independent European socialism.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call for a philosopher-elite and a revolutionary totalitarian state selected by merit and will; hereditary succession is not discussed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Freda wanted all material wealth owned by the state; user-owned cooperative banks are not mentioned and sit awkwardly with total state ownership.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the Western bourgeois system and a stance against liberal international order; IMF austerity is never discussed.

property-franchise.rationale: Freda sought to abolish private property and destroy the bourgeois liberal system, so a property-based franchise would be directly opposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The movement was elitist, hierarchical and anti-liberal; ecofeminist ideas are inferred to be foreign to it.

reification.rationale: Freda attacked bourgeois capitalism, which this claim echoes, but his critique was racial and elitist, not Marxist reification theory; adherents might split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the claim that bourgeois liberal freedoms are a facade for the ruling class, which Freda denounced while seeking a totalitarian alternative.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Freda proposed a totalitarian dictatorship ruled by an elite and rejected liberal legalism, so rule through binding standing laws is opposed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Nazi-Maoism took over far-right racial ideas, and its elitist state would reserve power to a racial elite; the sources stress race and hierarchy more than a formal franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: 1970s texts predate the internet, and an elite dictatorship rejects mass deliberation; inferred from its anti-democratic stance.

open-government-data.rationale: A conspiratorial elite dictatorship that rejects liberal accountability would not publish decision records for public scrutiny.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Freda's racial and spiritual hierarchy implies restrictions on mixing, but religion is not a central category in the sources; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement was hostile to Jews in the far-right tradition, but boycotts were not a documented tactic of this small revolutionary current.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Freda's antidemocratic rule by a philosopher-elite; popular deliberation by lot is never discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not address religious doctrine; adherents drew on pagan and traditionalist currents, so no clear answer can be inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call to abolish private property and destroy bourgeois liberal society, though concern for liberty is absent.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from far-right hierarchical and militarist ideas; openly serving gay soldiers is contrary to the milieu.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from Freda's traditionalist, Evolan influences, which are anti-materialist and not atheist promotion by the state.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the call for a totalitarian, hierarchical state under an elite, which depends on coercive power.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from totalitarian rule by a philosopher-elite, which leaves no space for communal power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Freda's state would own all material wealth, leaving no role for private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from rule by an elite rather than elected office, so term limits are not meaningful.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Gruppo di Ar manifesto declares 'We are antidemocratic' and rejects political parties.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources never discuss extinction risk; no basis for a direction.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical and traditionalist far-right side of the milieu.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the milieu's hierarchical, elitist and traditionalist family views.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Freda's racial hierarchy and rejection of democracy leave no room for non-citizens voting; inferred from his morphological racism and anti-democratic texts.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from his call for state ownership of material wealth; rent policy itself is never discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the abolition of private property in his programme; intellectual property is not mentioned.

uniformed-youth.rationale: A totalitarian, hierarchical fascist state mobilising youth is consistent with the movement's fascist model, though specific youth organisations are not documented.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its anti-American, anti-Western stance, which would oppose US-controlled weapons on European soil.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The movement was explicitly anti-American and sought to break Europe's subordination to the Atlantic bloc.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from Freda's hostility to Jews and the far-right milieu's minimising of the Holocaust; recognition is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: It attacked the bourgeoisie and proposed abolishing private property, so income from ownership would be rejected.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: It embraced Maoist people's war and political violence, which is incompatible with a ban on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its Evolian traditionalist sources and race-based thinking, though Freda's focus was a European rather than national identity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Freda's morphological racism, which treats biological types as fixed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, anti-egalitarian outlook; feminist theory is never discussed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The fascist and Evolian tradition it draws on honours heroic sacrifice for the cause.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Its Evolian traditionalist sources treat politics as a clash of metaphysical principles.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from its aim of a unified European state rather than a dispersed diaspora; not discussed directly.

culture-before-state.rationale: It stressed seizing power through people's war and destroying the system, so state-building came first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical traditionalist leanings, though it was not a Christian movement and the topic is not discussed.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, anti-egalitarian outlook, which would reject a feminist test of tradition.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its racial nationalism, though its state-ownership economics leaves the question mostly moot.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its racial-unity thinking; no specific territorial proposal is documented.

independent-unions.rationale: Freda's model is a totalitarian state; independent organisations of any kind would be incompatible with the proposed dictatorship.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nazi-Maoists called for a 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat' run by an elite, not real working-class self-rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call for state ownership of all material wealth.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of parliamentary forms; a hierarchical totalitarian state has no use for a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement demanded the abolition of private property in favour of state ownership, not local ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The proposed state is hierarchical and totalitarian, run by an elite, which excludes confederal local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Never addressed; wages are not discussed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian state's control of the economy; untraceable money would escape it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the totalitarian aims, which require political control; never discussed.

person-over-state.rationale: The state is totalitarian and the individual is subordinated to the community and its elite in the fascist element of the doctrine.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Freda drew on Evola and traditionalist spiritualism, as scholarship on his milieu notes; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from a centralised totalitarian state with no regional rights; powers would be held at the centre.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The racial elitist, Nazi element of the doctrine holds that races have distinct interests; the fascist side of the fusion is explicit.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial and ancestral pride belongs to the far-right half of the fusion, which rejects egalitarian internationalism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement glorified people's war and revolutionary violence, so defensive-only is inconsistent; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Freda's organic, racial view of European peoples as historical communities; language is not his stated criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: The movement wanted elections and parties abolished in favour of a unitary totalitarian state, which leaves no room for separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-American, anti-Soviet view that Europe was divided and held down by the two postwar blocs.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from its call to abolish private property and rebuild education under a state-run elite; free tuition fits, though it is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the movement favoured command by a totalitarian state over market-style taxes, and never addressed pollution.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from its organic, hierarchical view of a people's continuity across generations; the environmental sense was not addressed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from its virile, hierarchical, militarist outlook, which does not give women's values extra weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its embrace of Maoist people's war and a militarised totalitarian state.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: an elite-led totalitarian state would conduct foreign affairs by its own authority, not openly.

capital-controls.rationale: Abolishing private property and putting the economy under the state implies full state control of capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the milieu's embrace of armed minority struggle and people's war against the system, which would not accept a bourgeois state's arms monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the cult of struggle, hierarchy and discipline; adherents opposed pacifism and fought their own war against the system, though refusal against the Western system is plausible.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from Freda's totalitarian, hierarchical state owning wealth, which leaves no room for independent unions bargaining with employers.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from rejection of bourgeois welfare mechanisms that stabilise the capitalist order; the sources do not mention tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from a totalitarian state that would not accept legal limits on its economic power.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from violent anti-American and anti-Western stance and support for Third World liberation fronts; no concrete international economic programme is documented.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Freda sought to destroy the bourgeois liberal system and is characterised as anti-state in the existing form, to be replaced by a new totalitarian order.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Freda's state is totalitarian, hierarchical and owns all material wealth, leaving no room for pluralism about economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from Evolian traditionalist contempt for bourgeois materialism and the pricing of all things.

sacred-nation.rationale: Adherents were split between nation, race and a European or Eurasian civilisational unit; sacred Tradition matters more than any single nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The question belongs to reformist liberal politics that adherents want to destroy, not adjust; no position is documented.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the milieu's anti-colonial language was about America and the West, not regional inequality within states.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Freda held a morphological racism and elite hierarchy of natures, rejecting the universalist human dignity that the statement describes.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from a hostile view of the liberal press and a totalitarian state that would control media for its own purposes rather than keep it independent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Freda drew on Evola and Traditionalism, whose core thesis is a single primordial tradition behind the world's religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: Freda wanted a state economy with private property abolished and collective farming in the Maoist manner, which implies state-guaranteed farm security.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's militarism and hostility to American-led order; nuclear arms were not discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: the strand wanted a vanguard elite party leading the whole people and rejected parties as electoral fetishes, not a class-specific workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: the sources never touch the issue, and the strand's hostility to liberal universalism is offset by its totalitarian willingness to ban customs.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Freda's hierarchical, Evolian traditionalism, which favours distinct gender roles over equal-rights claims; property is also abolished in his scheme.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: no stated position, and the strand was European and pan-European in outlook with no language-classification theme.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Freda sought a total state with abolished private property, so pollution would be a matter for state command, not private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the strand wanted a philosopher-elite totalitarian state, not a consultative role for customary leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: individual liberty is despised, but the strand has no stated environmental doctrine and its aims are political, so adherents have no clear position.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the strand's authoritarian, anti-liberal state that would not leave sentencing to independent judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its ethnic-nationalist, anti-immigration tilt, which would demand assimilation of any who settle.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: Freda wanted all material wealth owned by a totalitarian state and unions are never discussed, so adherents have no clear position.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: Freda rejected parliamentary elections altogether, so voter registration rules are not a live question.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call for a hierarchical philosopher-elite state with one ordering vision, which would not tolerate competing interpretations having equal standing.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Freda's Gruppo di Ar manifesto states 'We are antidemocratic' and 'We are against political parties', rejecting competitive elections as the mark of legitimacy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: the sources cover the movement's elitist politics but not private sexual morality, and the far-right and Maoist strains differ here.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the aim of a totalitarian dictatorship that would suppress the liberal system and control public life.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Freda's abolition of private property and a state that owns all material wealth, which is incompatible with a market-style cash transfer.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical elite-rule model and rejection of democracy, under which equal voting and office rights for all would not hold.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the sources never discuss religion and women's oppression, and the strain's far-right and Maoist roots point opposite ways.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the far-right racial ideas the current drew on; the sources show racial thinking in Freda's circle, not rejection of race categories.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the anti-liberal, hierarchical stance; liberal equality bodies are part of the system it aimed to destroy.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Freda called for abolishing private property and state ownership of all material wealth, which leaves no room for first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Freda's hostility to the Western liberal system and its institutions; international courts are never discussed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the movement's elitist, philosopher-ruled totalitarian outlook; scripture is not a theme in the sources.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its centralised, hierarchical racial-elitist state, which would not write gender guarantees into group self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Freda's state ownership of all wealth; he would defend such a state, though rule by a philosopher-elite rather than a bureaucracy.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Freda's totalitarian hierarchy under an elite, which fits selection from above rather than direct popular vote.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the movement's revolutionary, anti-bourgeois stance; a privileged national church is not discussed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its call for a unified totalitarian state, which leaves little room for ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of liberal-democratic procedure in favour of an elite-led state; the issue is not discussed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources never address colonial borders; an anti-Western stance and a pan-European aim point in different directions.

simple-living.rationale: Maoist austerity points one way and Freda's cult of a strong, hierarchical order says nothing on lifestyle; the sources are silent.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; its racial-elitist outlook gives no clear lean on indigenous settlement restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from people's-war mobilisation, but the sources do not say whether women would be drafted.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Freda's blood-and-soil, ethnic-nationalist thought makes the people's bond to its land and ancestors central, per the quoted manifesto.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred only: adherents accepted political violence and totalitarian rule, but drug policy is never addressed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the Maoist anti-Western, anti-American orientation, which would favour closeness to China; adherents' China ties are only loosely documented.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from ethnic-nationalist ideas that a people is a community of blood beyond borders; not documented for kin minorities.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Freda's call for state ownership of all material wealth, which gives the state, not individuals owed compensation, control of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Freda's totalitarian, hierarchical state subordinates the individual wholly to the state and the elite, with no personal rights against it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is never discussed in the sources, and a state owning all wealth makes the question largely moot.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred only: a state owning all wealth could provide either way, and the sources do not discuss targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Freda's manifesto declares 'We are against political parties', which agrees, but the elite party-vanguard model he drew from Maoism still mediates between leader and people; the sources do not settle it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the anti-bourgeois stance and abolition of private property, which rejects business privileges of any kind.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the movement's intent to impose a unitary elite-led order gives no stated view on denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from Freda's fusion of a revolutionary modernizing state with traditional hierarchy and racial myth; not stated in this form.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and traditionalist and Maoist influences pull in opposite directions.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western, anti-capitalist stance and state ownership of all wealth, which implies national control of resources.

missingStatements.text: Europe should break free of American influence and the post-war liberal order.
missingStatements.rationale: Lutte du Peuple denounced the West and called for European Socialism, and adherents were violently anti-American.

missingStatements.text: Elections and political parties are fetishes of a failing system and should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Freda's Gruppo di Ar manifesto declares 'We are against political parties' and 'We are antidemocratic'.
missingStatements.declined: Parties and elections are rejected, but the profile answers organic-representation as split and the claim is specific to this fringe; existing anti-democratic statements (one-party-rule, direct-action) already place it.

missingStatements.text: A cultural revolution should uproot the values of the bourgeoisie.
missingStatements.rationale: Freda treated the bourgeoisie as the main enemy and called for a cultural revolution to root out its world, drawing on Maoist models.
missingStatements.declined: Maoist-specific "cultural revolution" framing; the bourgeoisie/class questions (class-struggle-history, profit-exploitation) already capture the substance and few other ideologies could take a side.

notes: Evidence base is small: the group lasted about five years and left few primary texts accessible online. Strands differ: Freda's Evolian traditionalism versus the Maoist mass-line emphasis of student militants. Many answers on social policy are low-confidence inferences.
